editorial:
Imagine waking up to find out that millions of people who have never met you are seeing your face in their dreams every single night. That is exactly what happens to Paul, a boring professor who just wants to be liked. At first, it feels like a dream come true because he becomes a global superstar for no reason. The movie has a weird, funny vibe that makes you wonder how you would handle sudden fame if you were just a regular guy with no special talents.

Nicolas Cage is amazing here because he plays the role of a confused, desperate man perfectly. The story moves quickly and takes a dark turn when the dreams start becoming scary, which keeps you guessing. While some parts feel a bit slow, the weirdness makes it worth your time.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Paul tries to control the dreams using a special machine. It backfires, and he starts appearing in nightmares, making the whole world hate him. In the end, the dream trend simply fades away. Paul ends up back where he started, but he is more broken and lonely than before. He has to face the fact that he is not special and that fame is just a fleeting, empty feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies and strange stories about fame.
